If you like Snow Crash, the sprawl trilogy by William Gibson is for you:

  • Neuromancer (1984)
  • Count Zero (1986)
  • Mona Lisa Overdrive (1988)

These are probably the most popular cyberpunk books, and for good reason.

I listened to the audio book a year or two ago and I agree, it was a lot of fun and many of the ideas are very relatable, relevant and a bit clever.

My favorite part was the terrifying and innocent nuclear powered robot guard dogs who can never stop moving because the violent winds being forced into their vents at impossible to follow speeds is the only thing keeping them from overheating and dying. The story felt like a young man's power fantasy and I loved it, kinda like a fun likable anime with a cute girl, semi-overpowered main character, doing his thing, saving the world and all. I also really liked what he had to say about great warriors as he deflected a spear without thinking about it. I could relate from what I've done in competitive games, and that's always fun to me.

There is a lot of cool cyberpunk ideas that this story gives you, funny little gadgets, tools, infrastructure and ways of life. Do it, read or listen to it, it's fun and will make you smile.
